_purpose: Every number the paper cites lives here once, with the run and artifact it is re-derived from. tools/constants/check.py and audit.py enforce it; tools/constants/export.py writes the paper's macros from it.

_schema.value: the number (or list, or an object where a reader indexes one number per key); null means not yet measured, and the note says why
_schema.card: the GPU the number is about, as the machine reported it; 'none' for a number about no card
_schema.context: the context length C the number was measured at; 'n/a' where it does not apply
_schema.timing_scope: one of _timing_scopes, or 'n/a' for a number that is not a time or a rate
_schema.run: measured only: the runs/<run-id> directory whose artifact the audit re-derives the value from
_schema.artifact: measured only: the file in that run directory
_schema.inputs: projected only: the constants keys the cost model read
_schema.note: one or two sentences; for external, the URL

_grades.measured: made by a driver in this repository; audit.py re-derives it from `artifact` in `run`
_grades.derived: arithmetic over other entries; check.py recomputes it from the entries it names
_grades.projected: the cost model, with the model's inputs named; never presented as a measurement
_grades.external: read from a public source, with its URL in the note
_grades.asserted: an assumption the owner made, with the reason in the note

_timing_scopes.commit: the commitment path only: interpolation, low-degree extension and Merkle hashing of the committed trees
_timing_scopes.stwo total: commit plus the prover's own call: constraint evaluation, quotients, out-of-domain sampling, FRI
_timing_scopes.whole wall: trace generation, interaction generation, stwo total and serialization, summed per segment; it does not include reading the witness or building the layer
_timing_scopes.loop: the one-process segment loop's own wall-clock time, which does include the witness read and the layer build; pipelined loops overlap one segment's generation with another's proving
_timing_scopes.primitive: one primitive of the proof system on its own (a hash, a field operation, a lookup, a fold), timed by the vendored library's benchmark harness; not a scope of any proof and not comparable with the four above
_timing_scopes.verify: the verifier's side, on the host's own cores and not on the card: one segment's call over its serialized statement, claims and proof, or the grid pass that checks the links between segments. It is not a scope of the prover and is not comparable with the four above.
_timing_scopes.unproved prefill: one `max_new_tokens=1` call on the unproved model with the weights already resident: the whole prompt read and the first generated position emitted. Nothing is proved in it.
_timing_scopes.unproved decode: the rest of the same full call, by difference: the remaining generated positions, one step each, with the weights already resident. Nothing is proved in it.
_timing_scopes.unproved end to end: the full call on its own: the prompt prefilled and every generated position decoded, as one wall-clock time, with the weights already resident. Nothing is proved in it.
_timing_scopes.extraction: the witness extraction: the forward passes that write the dumps the proofs read, on the card, timed by the driver around each pass. It is outside the prover, so it is in none of the four proving scopes; it does not include emitting the device kernels, installing them or rebuilding.
_timing_scopes.cold whole wall: the extraction the proofs read plus whole wall: what the sequence costs on a host that holds no witness dump yet. Kernel emission, the install and the rebuild are not in it.
_timing_scopes.cold loop: the extraction the proofs read plus loop: what the sequence costs on a host that holds no witness dump yet. Kernel emission, the install and the rebuild are not in it.

proof.headline.c4096.total_bytes.note: The serialized proofs of the sequence's 290 segments as the prover wrote them, added up: 18.46 GiB, one segment 48.4 to 120.0 MiB. It is the proof the prover produced: nothing compresses or aggregates it.

proof.headline.c4096.total_in_memory_byt.note: The same 290 proofs as the prover held them before serialization, added up from the run's 5 slice outputs: 7.19 GiB, 38.9 per cent of the serialized total. proof.headline.c4096.bytes_per_segment_m.note: The median segment's serialized proof, over the sequence's 290: 64.97 MiB, against 48.4 MiB for the smallest and 120.0 MiB for the largest. proof.headline.c4096.total_bytes / segments.headline.c4096, which is 65.20 MiB: what one segment of this sequence cost in serialized bytes on average. proof.headline.c4096.in_memory_bytes_per.note: The median segment's proof before serialization, over the sequence's 290: 25.33 MiB. The serialized median beside it is 2.56 times larger, which is the JSON encoding and not more proof.

proof.headline.c4096.total_in_memory_bytes / positions.headline.c4096, which is 1.60 MiB: the proof before serialization per proved position, 38.9 per cent of proof.headline.c4096.bytes_per_position. It is the whole sequence's verification spread over the positions it proves and is no one position's own time: the verifier is called once per segment.

commitment.c4096.sha256.note: The published model commitment: the digest of one line per layer coordinate carrying the layer number, that layer's model root and the model hash the root was derived under, and nothing else. It moves when the commitment moves and not when the file is reformatted.

commitment.c4096.layers.note: 32 layers and the output head's coordinate after them. One model root each, and the derivation refuses to write a table whose rows disagree about a layer's root.

commitment.c4096.cells.note: The (layer, prefix width) cells the table was derived over, one per segment of headline-c4096's plan. Every one of them was compared against the published commitment.

controls.suite.designed_rejections.note: Controls the verifier refused for the reason each was written for, over the suite's five targets: one real layer segment of headline-c4096's plan, that segment again under the --probe filter, and the three synthetic shapes. A control passes only as a designed rejection, with accepts false and falsified naming the verdict fields the bend turned off; a crash is never a pass and a skip by name is counted apart.

controls.suite.accepted.note: Controls the verifier accepted, over the same five targets, counted from every target's own probe record. Any number but zero is a soundness failure, and the run's gate fails on it.

controls.suite.crashes.note: Targets whose process died rather than finishing its list. A crash is never a pass: the gate fails the run on one, and each target's exit code is recorded beside its output so a run that dies is visible as a crash and not as a missing file.

controls.real.c4096.designed_rejections.note: Controls refused as designed on the real segment: layer 16 of the last token block of headline-c4096's plan, proved from that plan's own line. The suite had never finished on a real segment before: at 32e8fae it died at the control after the one that moves three values off the master table, taking the 41 refusals before it (zk-prover #134).

controls.real.c4096.skipped_by_name.note: Controls the prover skipped on the real segment by name, with the reason in the record: the attention-output seam's and the model swap's. Both rebuild the segment around a second draw of the residual stream, which is the synthetic construction's, so on a dump the draw and not the binding under test is what a refusal would be about (zk-prover #24). A control skipped by name is not a control that passed, which is why it is counted apart from the rejections.

segments.control.c4096.note: The same 290 segments as the headline row: 9 token blocks of 32 layer segments and an output head segment over the last prompt block and over the generated block. A control that proved one segment fewer would price that segment as well.

cells.control.c4096.fresh.note: Fresh committed cells over the same 290 segments with the five GKR reductions off, added up from the run's 5 slice outputs. The pair with cells.headline.c4096.fresh is what prices the reductions; the seconds of the two runs are not a pair, because this loop proves one segment at a time and the headline row's overlaps two.

secs.control.c4096.serial_loop.note: The segment loop's own wall-clock time with one segment in flight, summed over the run's 5 processes. Not comparable with secs.headline.c4096.loop, which is pipelined: over one sample the memory probe measured 228.738 s serial against 175.797 s pipelined for the same segments.

mem.control.c4096.peak_mib.note: The most the card reported holding at any moment of the segment loop, sampled once a second, with one segment in flight. The card has 81,559 MiB; the same plan with the reductions on peaks at 73,723 MiB, and with them off and two segments in flight it ran out of memory in token block 3 (zk-results #74).

gkr.control.c4096.leave_frac_cells.note: 1 - cells.headline.c4096.fresh / cells.control.c4096.fresh: the fraction of the committed cells the five reductions remove over a whole sequence at this context. gkr.ablation.all_five.leave_frac_cells is the same fraction on 32 segments of the block with the longest prefix, where the reductions weigh most.

segments.probe.c16384.note: The segments the two compared loops proved: layers 1 to 4 of the last token block, whose prefix is the whole 16,384-token prompt. They are the shape 1,023 of the headline plan's 1,056 segments have; layer 0's is the other one and is measured on its own.

cells.probe.c16384.fresh.note: Fresh committed cells over those four segments; 2.267 G each on average, against 1.251 G for the average segment of the context 4,096 sequence. The pipelined loop committed the same cells and produced the same four proof digests.

mem.probe.c16384.serial_peak_mib.note: The most the card reported holding at any moment of the loop with the pipeline off, sampled once a second. The card has 81,559 MiB. The prover's own high-water mark for the same loop is 75,894,751,232 bytes, which is this number to the MiB.

mem.probe.c16384.pipelined_peak_mib.note: The same four segments with the pipeline on, which holds two segments at once. It peaked at the same number as the loop that holds one, so at this context the second segment in flight cost the card nothing.

mem.probe.c16384.layer0_peak_mib.note: Layer 0 of the same block, proved on its own. Its statement carries the embedding gadget, which no other layer's does, and it is the largest segment of the headline plan: 6,464 MiB above the others and 2,716 MiB below the card.

secs.probe.c16384.serial_loop.note: The loop's own wall-clock time over four segments with the pipeline off: 57.18 s a segment, against 12.82 s at context 4,096 where the segments are a third of the size.

secs.probe.c16384.pipelined_loop.note: The same four segments with the pipeline on: 43.95 s a segment, 23.1 per cent less than the loop that holds one segment, for the same committed cells and the same four proof digests.

mem.probe.c16384.pipelined_l0_peak_mib.note: Layer 0 and layer 1 together under the pipeline, which is the pair the headline loop forms at the start of every block and the only pair that holds the plan's largest segment. It peaked at what layer 0 peaked at alone, so the second segment in flight cost the card nothing even here.

secs.probe.c16384.layer0_loop.note: Layer 0 of the last block, proved on its own with the pipeline off: one segment, and the slowest in the plan as well as the largest.

secs.probe.c16384.pipelined_l0_loop.note: Layers 0 and 1 under the pipeline: 75.31 s a segment against 94.67 s for layer 0 alone, so the pipeline helps on the pair that holds the largest segment too.

cells.microbench.compose_fresh.note: Fresh committed cells of the one synthetic segment this run proves, the prover's recorded sound shape with the five GKR reductions on. It is the denominator of the commitment rate below and nothing else; a segment this size is not a throughput row.

secs.microbench.compose_commit.note: The commitment path of that proof on the reference backend: interpolation, low-degree extension and Merkle hashing of the committed trees. Its low-degree test took 1.989 s of the same proof and its whole prove call 4.835 s.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_cells_per_a.note: Dequantization by a power-of-two scale, the marginal cells one accumulator adds with the shared tables left out; 1,048,576 accumulators, 16 per row. The tables are a fixed cost of the segment and are not multiplied by a count, which is why the marginal figure and not the with-tables one is the cost model's input.

model_constants.dequant_chain_cells_per_.note: Dequantization by the bf16 chain, on the same sweep and the same terms as the power-of-two row above. It costs 1.73 times as much per accumulator.

model_constants.attnout_int8_cells_per_a.note: The attention output's own dequantization, folded straight to int8 because its consumer requantizes it anyway: one rounding per output element, on the same sweep and the same terms as the two rows above. The cost model multiplies it by the attention outputs of every layer and head.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_cells_per_a.note: The part of the power-of-two dequantization that one accumulator costs whatever the row width is. The sweep proves the same 1,048,576 accumulators at 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 per trace row and every point is exactly 15 + 1/width marginal cells, so this is a closed form read off six measurements and not a fit; the row term is the entry below. At the 16-per-row layout the other subcommands use the two give 15.0625, which is the measured power-of-two figure above.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_cells_per_r.note: What a trace row of the power-of-two dequantization costs on top of its accumulators, from the same six-width sweep: one cell, spread over the accumulators the row carries. It is a property of the variant and not of the gadget in general -- on the same sweep's terms the bf16 chain carries two cells a row and the integer reading and the rounding carry none.

model_constants.requant_cells_per_value.note: One requantized value with its scale argument, the marginal cells with the shared tables left out and the two committed input cells left out because the producer commits them. The subcommand proves four points: 8.0625 and 11.4375 for power-of-two scales without and with the argument, 8.125 and 11.5 for bf16. The cost model takes the largest of the two with the argument and charges one less than it per distinct matmul input, because the committed quantized value is already counted.

model_constants.residual_stream_add_cell.note: One correctly rounded bf16 add of the residual stream, the marginal cells with the shared tables and the component's leaves left out. The cost model multiplies it by the two residual adds of every layer and by the adds of each normalisation's reduction. Putting a unary operation in front of the add does not move it: the same 24.3226 with a square on every leaf.

model_constants.residual_stream_mul_cell.note: One bf16 multiply of the residual stream, on the same terms as the add above. The cost model multiplies it by the two multiplies of every normalisation and by the SwiGLU's product. The SiLU in front of the product does not move it, and the normalisation's own scale is 8.4375 because its second operand is a preprocessed weight.

model_constants.argmax_cells_per_compari.note: Proving the emitted token is the argmax costs one comparison per vocabulary entry per token, and this is what one comparison costs: 8 tokens over a vocabulary of 8,192, 64 comparisons a row, of which 3.046875 cells are the committed trace and the rest the lookups. It is the whole gadget over the comparisons; the cost model subtracts an assumed fixed table half of 40,960 cells to reach a per-comparison marginal of 8.421875, and one vocabulary cannot separate the two -- a second one would.

model_constants.attention_cells_per_head.note: What one entry of the attention score grid costs: the committed shift, the exponential's answer and the probability, over 512 tokens and 1,024 keys at head dimension 64. It is exactly 4 at all five instance counts the run packs, 1 through 16, so it is the grid's own price and not an artefact of one packing. It is the whole of the attention term only in the superseded single-slope form; the key tile coefficients are what the cost model charges, and they carry a per-key and a per-token cost this number does not.

model_constants.weight_freivalds_cells_p.note: The weight Freivalds check's committed cells per weight, at the prover's own default row width: `result.points[0].cells.cells_per_weight` of runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b3-freivalds.json. Its three QM31 accumulator columns cost 12 cells a trace row and a row carries p weights, so the law is 12/p and p is a layout knob, not a constant of the gadget: this is 12/136, the default of `params_of`. The sweep beside it, b3-freivalds-widths.json, returns 12/p to the cell at 8, 16, 32 and 64 weights a row, which is what says the closed form holds rather than assuming it. A group of n matmuls shares one accumulator and so costs (4 + 8n)/(n p) per weight and not 12/p, which the cost model does not know: charging 12/p across a layer over-charges the two-matmul group by 20 per cent and the three-matmul one by 29. The private archive's 0.0902 is 12/133, the same law at a shape whose grid padded 32,256 rows up to 2^15, so it is this figure inflated 2.3 per cent by row padding and not a second measurement; this subcommand refuses a ragged tiling and reports the unpadded form.

model_constants.weight_freivalds_preproc.note: The preprocessed side of the same check at the same row width, the trace a proof reads once rather than commits again: `result.points[0].cells.preprocessed_per_weight` of runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b3-freivalds.json. It is exactly 1 + 4/p -- one cell a weight, plus the four selectors amortised over a row -- at 8, 16, 32, 64 and 136 weights a row, so it is the same closed form as the fresh figure beside it. Each point is a marginal over the weights two output widths differ by and carries no row padding; the private archive's 1.0903 is one padded component divided by its weights, from a component that also carried nine preprocessed columns beside its weights where this one carries four. The preprocessed trace is in none of the cost model's cell totals, so this figure moves `moe.<model>.preprocessed_over_fresh` and nothing else.

model_constants.logup_marginal_cells_per.note: The marginal cells one LogUp lookup adds, per lookup batch size: `result.closed_form.marginal_cells_per_lookup` of runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/logup.json and the four points beside it. 4 at batch 1, which every shared table's own side finalizes with, and 2 at batch 2, which every use side does, so it is 4/batch at both sizes this prover uses. Measured on a range check, one committed cell a lookup, and on a pair table lookup, two; the two agree, because an interaction column is one QM31 whatever the relation's arity, so the arity moves what the gadget commits and not the column count. Recorded as an object keyed by the batch size written as a string, because the cost model indexes it by the batch it charges and `cost_model.logup_marginal_by_batch` refuses a scalar.

model_constants.dequant_chain_away_cells.note: Dequantization by the bf16 chain at the rounding away from zero, the marginal cells one accumulator adds with the shared tables left out; 1,048,576 accumulators, 16 per row, from the `chain` point's `cells_per_acc_marginal` in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json. This is what the cost model charges on all seven layer matmuls, because rounding away from zero is what the quantization configuration specifies and what every recorded proof builds. `model_constants.dequant_chain_cells_per_acc` is the same gadget at the round half to even, 26.125, exactly one cell an accumulator more, and is not this.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_away_cells_.note: Dequantization by a power-of-two scale at the rounding away from zero, on the same sweep and the same terms as the chain entry above, from the `pow2` point's `cells_per_acc_marginal` in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json. The cost model charges it on the output head. `model_constants.dequant_pow2_cells_per_acc` is the round half to even, 15.0625, again exactly one cell an accumulator more.

model_constants.dequant_chain_away_base_.note: The chain variant's committed columns alone, with the LogUp running sums left to the batched reduction: `columns.base` of the same `chain` point in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json, 230 columns over the 16 accumulators a trace row carries. That is what a proof with `--gkr-dequant` builds, which is the configuration the paper reports. The round-half-to-even output gives 246/16 = 15.375, one cell an accumulator more, the same difference as on the marginal figures.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_away_base_c.note: The power-of-two variant's committed columns alone, on the same terms as the chain entry above: `columns.base` of the `pow2` point in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json, 148 columns over 16 accumulators a row. Of the four away figures this is the one the sound statement charges most, because with `--gkr-dequant` on the layer matmuls read the composed price instead and the output head's dequantization is this. The round-half-to-even output gives 164/16 = 10.25.

model_constants.argmax_marginal_cells_pe.note: What one argmax comparison adds, as the slope of fresh cells against comparisons over three vocabularies at the same 8 tokens and the same 64 comparisons a row: 592,896 cells over 65,536 comparisons in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b10-argmax.json (vocabulary 8,192), 858,112 over 131,072 in b10-argmax-v16k.json and 1,388,544 over 262,144 in b10-argmax-v32k.json, each the strict point's `cells.fresh`. The three are exactly collinear: 4.046875 cells a comparison, and a fixed side of 327,680 cells -- 65,536 of committed trace and 262,144 of interaction -- that does not move with the vocabulary. This is the figure the cost model charges. `model_constants.argmax_cells_per_comparison` is the whole gadget over its comparisons, 9.046875 at the smallest of the three vocabularies, and is not this; subtracting an assumed fixed side of ten interaction columns over the trace rows, which is what the model did until this run, gives 8.421875 and is wrong by the whole of the real fixed side. The private archive's 4.046875 is this same number.

model_constants.int8_range_cells_per_act.note: model_constants.logup_marginal_cells_per_lookup['2'] / 2. The range check on a committed int8 activation is one arity-2 lookup into the 2^16 byte-pair table covering two activations, at the batch size every use side finalizes with; the activations' own committed cells are charged elsewhere. The private archive measured the same 1.0 directly at three sizes, and the byte-at-a-time form it replaced is 2.0.

model_constants.residual_stream_unary_ce.note: 2 + model_constants.logup_marginal_cells_per_lookup['2']. One bf16 unary operation commits its output as one bf16 value, which is two cells, and pays one lookup at pairwise batching. The cost model multiplies it by each normalisation's square and inverse square root and by the SwiGLU's SiLU. The prover reports the same figure under primitives.unary of the residual-stream output, built from the same two terms, so it is an exact count and not a second measurement.

model_constants.dequant_chain_composed_c.note: What the composed prover builds the whole dequantization at, per matmul accumulator: 353,632,256 cells over 22,020,096 accumulators, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are the committed columns (`family_cells.dequant`) plus what the reduction leaves in the interaction trace (`family_cells.interaction_by_family.dequant.cells`); the accumulators are the segment's own `family_cells.mats[].n` added up. The committed accumulator is in it and the cost model charges that separately as well. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.dequant_chain_cells_per_acc` is the standalone chain gadget, 26.125 cells with the round half to even, and must not be read for this. Both segments record `params.round: "even"`, so this is the round-half-to-even figure; on the layer matmuls the cost model charges rounding away from zero, which is one cell an accumulator less.

model_constants.requant_composed_cells_p.note: What the composed prover builds the whole requantization at, per distinct matmul input value: 212,664,832 cells over 11,534,336 values, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are the committed columns of the three seams (`family_cells.requant[].cells.base`), the multiplicity column of their own tables (`family_cells.requant_tables.multiplicity`) and the interaction the reduction leaves (`family_cells.interaction_by_family.requant.cells`); the values are `family_cells.requant[].checked` added up. The committed int8 value and its range check are the producer's and are not in it. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.requant_cells_per_value` is the standalone gadget, 11.5, and is not this.

model_constants.quant_composed_cells_per.note: What the composed prover builds the quantization of the attention q and k at, per value: 45,875,200 cells over 2,621,440 values, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are `family_cells.quant[].cells.base` plus `family_cells.interaction_by_family.quant.cells`, the values `family_cells.quant[].checked` added up. No reduction owns this one and no other key names it: until the composed statement was priced the cost model charged nothing for it at all. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own.

model_constants.weight_freivalds_compose.note: What the composed prover builds the Freivalds check of the weight matmuls at, per weight: 44,040,192 cells over 218,103,808 weights, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are `family_cells.freivalds` plus `family_cells.interaction_by_family.freivalds.cells`, the weights `family_cells.freivalds_weights[].weights` added up. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. The standalone check is 0.0902 cells a weight at its own design point in the width sweep the cost model still reads from a retired benchmark tree, and the composed check at this statement is more than twice that, most of the difference interaction the reduction does not remove. `model_constants.weight_freivalds_cells_per_weight`, which `microbench-cells` is to measure, is that standalone figure and is not this.

model_constants.attnout_composed_cells_p.note: What the composed prover builds the attention-output fold at, per accumulator: 21,757,952 cells over 2,097,152 accumulators, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are `family_cells.attnout` plus `family_cells.interaction_by_family.attnout.cells`; the accumulators are the segment's own `params.nh` x `params.hd` x `params.s`, which is the `family_cells.attnout_stats.n` the segment reports. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.attnout_int8_cells_per_acc` is the standalone fold, 10.0625, and is not this.

model_constants.residual_stream_composed.note: What one bf16 multiply of the residual stream costs in the composed prover: 26,214,400 cells over 5,242,880 multiplies, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. Read off the rope's own two multiplies per rotated value, the `rpqm` and `rpkm` entries of `family_cells.residual_stream_components`, whose `cells` and `ops` the segment reports on their own; they are the only bf16 multiplies a segment counts by themselves. These are the committed columns alone: the 163,840 cells the reduction leaves for the two components are not in it. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.residual_stream_mul_cells_per_op` is the standalone multiply, 8.75, and is not this.

What one bf16 add of the residual stream costs in the composed prover: 47,185,920 cells over 2,621,440 adds, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. Read off the rope's own add per rotated value, the `rpqa` and `rpka` entries of `family_cells.residual_stream_components`, on the same terms as the multiply above: the committed columns alone, without the 163,840 cells the reduction leaves for the two components. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.residual_stream_add_cells_per_op` is the standalone add, 24.3226, and is not this.

What one SwiGLU channel costs in the composed prover, one `silu` table application and one bf16 product together: 73,400,320 cells over 7,340,032 channels, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. Read off the `gsw` entry of `family_cells.residual_stream_components`, the committed columns alone, without the 196,608 cells the reduction leaves for it. The table application on its own is this less the multiply beside it, 5. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. attention_grid.base_cell_coeffs.unit: cells per S*C, per C, per S
attention_grid.base_cell_coeffs.note: The prefix key tile's committed cells at the 8B model's attention width, as the (S*C, C, S) triple the cost model reads: cells = 64 S C + 12288 C + 128 S. Solved from the three points above, whose key tiles cost 64 (S C + S^2) + 12288 C + 12416 S in total; the triple is that total under the composition the cost model itself uses, a prefix key tile at (S, C) plus the same tile at (S, S) with the per-token component dropped. Every coefficient is an identity of the layout at 32 heads of 128: 64 is two per head, 12288 is three per head and channel, 128 is four per head. With the context equal to the block length the C and S columns are the same quantity, so the point at a block of 256 with a prefix of 4,096 is what separates them; three points and three coefficients is an exact solve, so the residual is zero by construction and is not a check of the form. The proofs are made on the host's cores under the reference backend and the card is idle throughout; the machine reports an H200, which is what the run id names, and no timing figure from this run is recorded. A cell count does not depend on the card.

secs.headline.c4096.extract.note: The five layer passes over the whole sequence, added up: the job extracts the whole witness set once and then proves it. The head dumps are one further pass and the driver does not time it, so it is not in this number.

secs.headline.c16384.extract_prove.note: The prove sweep's extraction, added up over the seven groups of token blocks: the extraction whose dumps the 1,058 proofs read. The witness set does not fit the host at this context, so the job extracts a group, proves it and deletes it; a group extracted twice counts once, at its last extraction, which is why this is 9,735 s and not the 9,683 s of the first pass's seven rows in groups.jsonl. The head dumps are one further pass and the driver does not time it.

secs.headline.c16384.extract_survey.note: The survey sweep's extraction, added up over the same seven groups. This run extracted twice: an emitter reads a segment's dump to lower its shape, so the kernels have to be emitted while the dumps are there, and the survey sweep is the pass that writes the shape tables and emits the kernels. It is what the grouping arrangement costs and no proof reads its dumps, so the cold rows do not count it.

secs.headline.c4096.cold_whole_wall.note: secs.headline.c4096.extract + secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall. What the sequence costs on a host that holds no witness dump yet: the extraction the proofs read and the proving scope, one after the other. Emitting the device kernels, installing them and rebuilding are not in it, and no artifact of this run times them.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.intera.note: The interaction tree: the LogUp numerator and denominator columns of every gadget in the segment. cells_per_position.headline.c4096.bounda.note: The boundary trees, which commit the residual stream and the keys and values a segment hands to the segment that reads it. The chunk's cells object does not name them: they are what fresh has above base and interaction, which is how the audit reads them. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096; base, interaction and boundary add up to cells.headline.c4096.fresh and shape and model to the preprocessed cells beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.model.note: The model tree, one of the two preprocessed trees: the weights the segment reads. It is preprocessed and is therefore not part of fresh. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096; base, interaction and boundary add up to cells.headline.c4096.fresh and shape and model to the preprocessed cells beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.shape.note: The shape tree, the other preprocessed tree: the lookup tables and the constants the segment's shape fixes. It is preprocessed and is therefore not part of fresh. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096; base, interaction and boundary add up to cells.headline.c4096.fresh and shape and model to the preprocessed cells beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base_a.note: The base trace's share belonging to the attention output's dequantization, folded straight to int8 because the requantize seam after it quantizes it again. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096. The nine components and cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattributed add up to cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base, and the interaction tree is split beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base_d.note: The base trace's share belonging to the dequantization after each matmul, the bf16 chain and the power-of-two scales together. The chunk's `mats` list is this same count split per matmul and is not a component beside it. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096. The nine components and cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattributed add up to cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base, and the interaction tree is split beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base_e.note: The base trace's share belonging to the embedding lookup that binds a block's first residual stream to the ids the statement publishes. Only a layer-0 segment states it, one per token block, and the chunk reports no embedding object on the others; it is 12,304 cells a position at both contexts because a block embeds its own 512 positions and no prefix. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096. The nine components and cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattributed add up to cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base, and the interaction tree is split beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base_f.note: The base trace's share belonging to the weight matmuls, checked by Freivalds' method: the check's own accumulator columns, not the weights, which are preprocessed and are cells_per_position.headline.c4096.model. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096. The nine components and cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattributed add up to cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base, and the interaction tree is split beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base_k.note: The base trace's share belonging to the attention scores over the key tiles, the diagonal block among them. It is the one component that grows with the prefix a block reads, which is why the two contexts are not the same shape. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096. The nine components and cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattributed add up to cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base, and the interaction tree is split beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base_q.note: The base trace's share belonging to the quantization of q and k. It is 1,146,880 cells a position at both contexts: a layer quantizes its own 512 positions and the two output head segments state none. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096. The nine components and cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattributed add up to cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base, and the interaction tree is split beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base_r.note: The base trace's share belonging to the requantization at the qkv, gateup and down seams, and to the multiplicity columns of the tables those seams look in, which the chunk reports beside the seams as `requant_tables`. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096. The nine components and cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattributed add up to cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base, and the interaction tree is split beside it.

The base trace's share belonging to the two normalisations, the residual adds and the rope reconstructions. The chunk's `residual_stream_components` list is this same count split per component and is not a component beside it. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096. The nine components and cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattributed add up to cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base, and the interaction tree is split beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base_t.note: The base trace's share belonging to the LogUp tables: the multiplicity column each of them commits, over the exponential, the reciprocal, the range checks and the residual stream's own tables. The chunk gives every table its row count and its key columns and no cell count, so the audit charges one column of its rows; what fixes the column at one is that the components then close to the segment's own base tree exactly, on every segment that states no argmax. The interaction side of the same tables is four columns and is cells_per_position.headline.c4096.interaction_table. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096. The nine components and cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattributed add up to cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base, and the interaction tree is split beside it.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.unattr.note: The base trace's cells no counter names: 131,727,360 on each of the two output head segments, none on any of the 288 layer segments, and the same integer at both contexts because a head segment reads its block's own positions and no prefix. It is the argmax gadget's base side, which proves the emitted token is the lowest-indexed maximum of the logits: the chunk's `interaction_split` prices the same gadget's interaction side at 1,012 columns over 131,072 rows and this is 1,005 columns over the same rows, one value short of two cells per comparison on either side. `family_cells` emits a bare integer for every other component of the base trace and none for the argmax, so the audit records the cells rather than attributing them. Added up over the run's slice outputs and divided by positions.headline.c4096; it is not the 8,388,608-cell gap between a segment's fresh and its base and interaction trees, which is the boundary trees and is cells_per_position.headline.c4096.boundary.

cells_per_position.headline.c4096.fresh_.note: The fresh cells of the 32 layer segments of one token block over the 512 positions that block proves: 44,557,347,792 cells over 512, block B8, the one block of the sequence whose prefix is the whole context. It is what the cost model's registration compares its layers-only prediction per decoded token against, and the block is the comparison the prediction means: the model prices 32 layers at the full context, where the earlier blocks of the sequence read a shorter prefix and cost less. The output head segment is not in it; layer segment B8L0 is, with the embedding lookup and the one extra cell an attention-output accumulator it carries, 41,168 cells a position between them. The same 32 segments proved again for the reduction ablation come to the same integer, `cells.ablation.c4096.all_five`. It is a larger figure than `cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base` and its two companions added up, which divide every segment of the run, output heads and short prefixes included, by every position the run proves.

e4.qwen2p5_14b.c4096.predicted_cells_per.note: The E4 prediction for Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct at context 4,096: fresh cells per decoded token over the model's 48 layer segments, layers only, at the statement tools/drivers/predict-14b.sh proves. Every segment is COUNTED from the prover's trace layout at the witness-calibrated fields of its own dump -- the master exponent table's size, the normalisation width and the attention output's five widths -- which are properties of the forward pass and exist before any proof of them does; runs/2026-09-11-register-14b-none/witness-fields.json holds them, one row per layer, and the registration names that file by digest. The 48 tables are 2^21 to 2^25 rows and not one size: a prediction that charges one, as the priced model does at the 8B's 2^23, is wrong by most of a table on the layers that are not 2^23, which is why this number moved from 151,193,309 when the owner ruled on 2026-09-11 that a model whose table size is known is priced at it. It is read out of runs/2026-09-11-register-14b-none/registration.json, whose prediction_sha256 is 406cf7e43961547cec58957ecd2042bc0085ae4d84efc6508810248ce4de3c37, and check.py re-reads that document on every run, because a registration is the one number here that must not move after it is made. No cell cost is charged on the committed side: nothing in this number is priced from a per-unit constant and no input comes from outside this repository and zk-prover. It was recorded before anything measured this shape, which is what makes it a prediction; the measured side and the ratio between them are not here yet, and are blocked on zk-prover #172 and #174.
